title: Anomalous weak values in a generalized Mach-Zehnder interferometer extracted directly from intensity measurements
authors: Ismaele V. Masiello, Hartmut Lemmel, Andreas Dvorak, Stephan Sponar, Yuji Hasegawa
abstract: Weak values provide a powerful framework for characterizing quantum systems. Their experimental extraction conventionally relies on weak conditioned von Neumann measurements, involving weak interactions and meter states that increase experimental complexity and often limit measurement efficiency. Here we introduce a method to fully characterize path weak-values in a generalized Mach-Zehnder interferometer employing neither meter states nor weak interactions. We experimentally demonstrate the technique in matter-wave interferometry. We identify anomalous weak values and, equivalently, negative quasiprobability distributions, which reflect the nonclassical behavior of the quantum system. The approach relies uniquely on intensity measurements at the output ports of the interferometer combined with controlled relative phase shifts between the paths. The absence of meter states enables considerable simplification of the setup and shorter measurement times, while preserving full access to weak values with comparable or increased accuracy. The scheme is directly applicable to a broad class of experiments involving two-level quantum systems.
summary: The paper presents an innovative method to measure path weak-values in a Mach-Zehnder interferometer using only direct intensity measurements, bypassing the need for complicated meter states or weak interactions. By analyzing these intensities, the researchers successfully identified anomalous weak values, providing experimental evidence of nonclassical quantum behavior and contextuality in matter waves.
main_problem: To characterize path weak-values in a generalized Mach-Zehnder interferometer without relying on complex techniques like meter states or weak interactions.
main_result: The authors successfully extracted path weak-values directly from intensity measurements, identifying anomalous values that confirm the nonclassical behavior and contextuality of the quantum system.
method: Weak values are derived by relating measured output intensities $I_{\pm}(\delta)$—obtained solely through controlled relative phase shifts $\delta$ at the interferometer outputs—to the path weak-values using specific equations.
model_or_system: The experiment uses a matter-wave interferometry setup, specifically a neutron Mach-Zehnder interferometer, modeling the system as a two-level quantum superposition of spatially separated paths.
key_observables: Path weak-values ($	ext{w}_{\pm,j}$), outgoing beam intensities $I_{\pm}(\delta)$, and single-beam path intensities ($I_{+,1}, I_{+,2}$).
important_parameters: Controlled relative phase shift ($\delta$), initial relative phase ($\phi$), contrast reduction factor ($C$).
main_assumptions: The analysis incorporates corrections for contrast reduction due to experimental imperfections and notes that the extraction method is sensitive to intensity measurements approaching zero.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the MZI setup, show sinusoidal modulation of intensities vs. phase shifts, and present plots comparing extracted weak values ($	ext{w}_R$ and $	ext{w}_I$) for both unbalanced (anomalous) and balanced configurations.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theory of weak values, details the generalized MZI setup, derives the relationship between measurable intensities and weak values, presents methods to handle experimental imperfections (contrast reduction), and finally demonstrates the extraction process using neutron interferometry data.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly practical, simplified measurement protocol for accessing fundamental quantum quantities like weak values in complex interferometers, which is crucial for testing foundational principles of quantum mechanics beyond standard measurements.
